newsitem.title: GREECE: OLYMPICS-IOC PRAISES GREEK POPULAR SUPPORT FOR ATHENS BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-IOC PRAISES GREEK POPULAR SUPPORT FOR ATHENS BID.

text.p: International Olympic Committee officials praised Greek popular support for Athens' bid to host the 2004 Games on Sunday, but stressed the race between the 11 candidate cities was only just starting.

"The commission has taken note of the support lent to the candidacy by the overwhelming majority of the Greek population," said IOC evaluation commission president Thomas Bach. "Now the marathon is on."

Greece buried its bitterness over losing the 1996 centenary Games to Atlanta and has returned with a new bid, based on its modern athletic infrastructure rather than its historic right as the birthplace of the Olympics 2,700 years ago.
A recent nationwide poll by the Athens bidding committee showed 96.4 percent of Greeks want the Olympics and thousands have already signed up as volunteers.
Bach also commended the support offered by the government and opposition parties to hosting the games as well as Greece's proposed "creative cultural programmes."

If it wins the Games, Athens plans to hold the marathon on its original course -- from the historic Marathon battlefield to the capital -- and relay the Olympic flame from ancient Olympia through all the significant cities of the ancient Greek world.
The IOC voted down Greece's bid for the 1996 Games because of poor infrastructure and lack of confidence that Athens could meet the demands of the Olympics.

Greek officials, who almost took for granted the IOC would opt to hold the 100th anniversary of the Games in the city where they were revived in 1896, were so incensed at losing to Atlanta they vowed never to bid again.
But they have since had a change of heart.

"This is a totally new bid with a totally new attitude," said bidding committee head Yanna Angelopoulou. "Eighty percent of the sports facilities are already in place and we have the money for the rest. We are proud of our Olympic heritage but we don't depend on it to win the Games."

The IOC will announce the destination of the 2004 Games in September. Athens, Rome, Stockholm and Cape Town are considered strong candidates. The other bidders are Buenos Aires, Istanbul, Lille, Rio de Janeiro, San Juan, Seville and St Petersburg.
